column3: NASB omits “answering”; it renders “fair weather” as “it will be fair weather.”

NASB has no “hypocrites,” like the critical text; “red and threatening” renders “red, being overcast,” and it repeats “discern.” The critical text marks vv. 2b–3 as doubtful, but NASB prints them without brackets.
NASB follows the critical text with “the sign of Jonah” without “the prophet.”
NASB adds “of the sea” and “any,” and has no “His,” like the critical text.
NASB follows the critical text (“you have no bread”) and adds “men” to “of little faith.”
NASB follows the critical text (“concerning bread … But beware”).
NASB follows the critical text without “Me”; “men” is rendered “people.”
“Will not prevail against” is rendered “will not overpower.”
NASB renders the future passives as future perfects: “shall have been bound,” “shall have been loosed.”
NASB follows the critical text with “the disciples” and “the Christ,” without “His” and “Jesus”; “ordered” is rendered “warned.”
“Far be it from You” (literally “mercy to You”) is rendered “God forbid it.”
“Your thoughts are not of the things of God” is rendered “you are not setting your mind on God’s interests.”
NASB renders “give” as “repay” and “each” as “every man”; the last clause is in capitals as an Old Testament quotation.
